Topic: Provide descriptive and unique page titles
Do: Ensure each page has a unique title.
Make title descriptive of page content.
Include brand name consistently in title.
Use concise and clear page titles.
Ensure title loads before user interaction.
Maintain title consistency across site sections.
Test title readability with screen readers.
Ensure titles are unique in browser tabs.
Add document title via <title> tag only once.
Check dynamic changes via JavaScript update document.title.
Dont: Don’t use generic titles like 'Home' or 'Page 1'.
Don’t use titles unrelated to content.
Don’t change title mid-navigation without reason.
Don’t use emojis or symbols as titles.
Don’t dynamically remove title on reload.
Don’t use title attributes instead of page titles.
Don’t let scripts overwrite correct titles.
Don’t mislead users with incorrect titles.
Don’t put version numbers in every title.
Don’t reuse same title in different modules.
Don’t include redundant punctuation in title.
Edge cases: SPA changes content but document.title remains old
Multiple title tags inserted by third-party script
Title updated after async content load but too late for screen reader
Iframe lacks title attribute or has generic title
CMS template sets identical title for product variations
Title localized incorrectly compared to on-page language
Browser caching shows an old title after deployment
Title contains invisible whitespace or control characters
Title truncated on mobile hiding critical info
Title set by meta robots or SEO tool instead of <title>
Popups that behave like pages lack distinct titles
Title includes encoded HTML entities rendering poorly
Title changed by analytics script unintentionally
Title missing for print/PDF export view
Title mismatch between server-rendered and client-rendered pages

Multilingual pages showing wrong title due to routing error
Title dynamically set then removed on error handling
Title exists but not within head due to template bug
Title uses unsupported characters causing encoding errors
